boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct CSUN University Library environments for quiet work, collaborative projects, technology-assisted study, tutoring, and accessible research.

cards.title: Set Up in the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Flexible individual and collaborative study on the main floor
cards.notes: Choose ergonomic seating for solo work or a group configuration for collaboration, then use the nearby research and technology support desks.
cards.short_summary: A flexible main-floor workspace with seating, computers, printing, and on-site research support.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN says the Learning Commons spans the University Library’s first floor and provides ergonomic individual seating, group configurations, desktop computers, printing, and research help.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons FAQ | CSUN University Library
cards.access_notes: The Learning Commons occupies the first floor. Library operating hours vary during the academic year; consult the current library-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Take a Pod in the Quiet Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Fourth-floor east-wing seating for focused individual work
cards.notes: Bring a charger-compatible device and settle into a pod or other individual seat; keep conversation and phone calls outside this quiet zone.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-designed quiet lounge with individual pods and furnishings equipped with built-in chargers.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN identifies the Quiet Study Lounge in the fourth-floor east wing as an individual-study space with pods and other furnishings that include built-in chargers.
cards.source_title: Library | California State University, Northridge Catalog
cards.access_notes: Located on the University Library’s fourth floor, east wing. This is a quiet individual-study area; talking and phone conversations are not allowed.

cards.entity_name: Robert and Maureen Gohstand Leisure Reading Room
cards.title: Read Quietly in the Gohstand Room
cards.subtitle: A second-floor west-wing room specifically designated for reading
cards.notes: Use this room when your task is sustained reading rather than discussion, and follow the library’s quiet-area rules while you work.
cards.short_summary: A named reading room set apart for quiet, text-focused study on the library’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN states that the Gohstand Leisure Reading Room is on the second floor in the west wing and provides a quiet space specifically designated for reading.
cards.source_title: Library | California State University, Northridge Catalog
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor, west wing. The library designates the room for quiet reading; follow posted library access and noise rules.

cards.title: Work Alongside Teaching and Media Collections
cards.subtitle: Second-floor east-wing space for study and collection-based research
cards.notes: Set up here when an assignment draws on teaching materials, juvenile literature, music, or media, and check service availability before seeking staff help.
cards.short_summary: A collection-centered study environment suited to education, music, and media coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN describes the Teacher Curriculum Center/Music & Media on the second-floor east wing as an environment for study, research, relaxation, and personal enjoyment.
cards.source_title: Library | California State University, Northridge Catalog
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor, east wing. Service-point hours may differ from building hours, so verify current availability before requesting materials or assistance.

cards.title: Pair Study Time with Academic Support
cards.subtitle: Third-floor east-wing tutoring and writing support
cards.notes: Bring the assignment, course instructions, and a working draft or problem set; schedule ahead when possible, since walk-in help is not guaranteed.
cards.short_summary: An academic-support setting for writing consultations, subject tutoring, workshops, and collaborative learning.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN locates the Learning Resource Center on the University Library’s third-floor east wing and says it provides tutoring, supplemental instruction, writing support, and workshops.
cards.access_notes: The LRC maintains a schedule separate from the University Library. Writing Center appointments are strongly recommended, though walk-in or drop-in sessions may be available.

cards.title: Reserve a Room for Solo Focus
cards.subtitle: Enclosed individual rooms on the second, third, and fourth floors
cards.notes: Reserve a north-side room online or look for a first-come south-wall room; use the room alone and retain your confirmation during the session.
cards.short_summary: Single-user rooms offering a more enclosed setting than the library’s open study floors.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN says individual study rooms are on floors two through four; north-side rooms on floors two and three require reservations, while south-wall rooms are first-come, first-served.
cards.access_notes: For CSUN students only and limited to one occupant. Reservations require an @csun.edu or @my.csun.edu address and may be made up to two days ahead.

cards.title: Book a Room for the Group Project
cards.subtitle: Reservable collaborative rooms across floors one through four
cards.notes: Gather at least two students, reserve with a CSUN email, confirm promptly, and arrive within ten minutes so the group does not forfeit the slot.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed collaborative rooms intended for student teams working together on projects and coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN provides group study rooms in the Learning Commons and on upper floors, dedicates them to groups of two or more CSUN students, and requires online reservations.
cards.access_notes: CSUN student groups of at least two may reserve up to two days ahead. Reservations require confirmation, and the room is forfeited after a ten-minute no-show.

cards.title: Use an Accessibility-Equipped Study Room
cards.subtitle: Adjustable workstations and assistive software in the Learning Commons
cards.notes: Complete DRES equipment training first, then present the issued card at Guest Services to obtain a room key for an accessibility-supported session.
cards.short_summary: Three dedicated rooms with adjustable furniture, assistive software, scanning, magnification, and text-to-speech tools.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN says rooms LC-5 through LC-7 contain adjustable tables, ergonomic chairs, computers, OCR scanning, magnification, text-to-speech systems, and assistive software.
cards.source_title: Assistive Technology Rooms | CSUN University Library
cards.access_notes: Limited to CSUN students registered with DRES and trained on the equipment. Present the DRES card at Guest Services to check out a key for up to three hours per day.

cards.title: Move to the Fourth-Floor Quiet Core
cards.subtitle: Open quiet-study seating among the library’s upper-level collections
cards.notes: Choose this floor for individual work, silence devices, and move to floors one through three or a stairwell before taking a phone conversation.
cards.short_summary: A broad quiet-study option for students who prefer open seating over an enclosed room.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN designates the fourth-floor core as quiet study and states that the fourth floor also contains study areas plus graduate, group, and individual study rooms.
cards.access_notes: The fourth-floor core is governed by the library’s quiet-study policy: no talking or phone conversations, no amplified media, and headphones at low volume.

cards.title: Put the Group’s Screen on Display
cards.subtitle: Technology-enabled collaboration tables in designated study areas
cards.notes: Bring an HDMI-ready device or borrow a compatible adapter from Library Technology Services, then mirror shared material for the group to review.
cards.short_summary: Collaborative tables that connect personal devices to a shared monitor for presentations and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN says Media Scape tables in designated collaborative study areas let users connect personal devices to an HD monitor for group work and discussion.
cards.access_notes: Located in technology-supported collaborative areas in the Learning Commons and on the second floor. Adapter checkout depends on Library Technology Services availability.
